title: Remove Extra Spaces Between Words
statement:
You are given a sentence in which words may be separated by more than one space. A **word** is a maximal run of non-space characters.

Rewrite the sentence so that:

- consecutive words are separated by exactly **one** space, and
- there are no spaces at the beginning or at the end.

The characters inside each word, and the order of the words, must not change. Print the cleaned sentence.
input_format: A single line containing the sentence. It may start or end with spaces and may contain runs of spaces.
output_format: Print the cleaned sentence on one line.
constraints: `s` contains printable ASCII characters (no tabs or other control characters) and at least one non-space character

examples.explanation: The leading and trailing spaces are removed and every gap between words shrinks to a single space.
A single word needs no changes.
Runs of four and five spaces both collapse to one.

hints: Scan the line once and decide for each character whether it belongs in the output.
Copy non-space characters as they are. Write a space only if the previous written character is not a space and something has already been written.
After the scan, a pending trailing space (if any) must be dropped. Two pointers (read and write) also let you do this in place.
